issues.description: Person 'first name' identifier is inconsistent across artifacts. The problem statement and the template common model define the attribute and accessors as 'firstName' (getFirstName()/setFirstName()) and the client views/controllers (PersonScene, PersonController) and server service (PersonService) expect that name. In the solution repository the common Person model instead declares the field and accessors as 'givenName' (getGivenName()/setGivenName()). This naming divergence means code that calls getFirstName()/setFirstName() (e.g. PersonService.savePerson, PropertyValueFactory("firstName") in PersonScene) will not find matching accessors on the solution Person class, causing compilation errors or runtime binding failures and preventing students from compiling and running the project as presented.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the 'first name' identifier consistent across all artifacts. Prefer restoring the identifier used in the template/problem statement: rename the solution repository's Person.givenName field and its accessors to firstName, getFirstName(), setFirstName(). Update the solution Person.java accordingly so its API matches PersonService, controllers, and views. Alternatively, if you prefer 'givenName', update all callers (PersonService, PersonController, PersonScene, and the problem statement) to use getGivenName()/setGivenName() and the property name 'givenName' consistently. Restoring 'firstName' in the common model is the least disruptive fix for students following the template and specification.
